summary: Forest Service lookout planned for Hamilton Mountain near Merritt in 1951; now surrounded by private land with no public access.

facts.status_note: A travel guide lists it as believed still standing; no source describes its condition.
facts.design: Planned as a permanent pre-fabricated building, with a tent used first

access.note: Surrounded by private property; landowners have stopped public access up the service road. Firelookout.ca: private property, no access.

events.note: Planned in May 1951 and expected to be in operation in July 1951, per the Merritt Herald as reproduced by Canada Lookouts. Completion is not confirmed by these sources.

evidence.supports: The B.C. Forest Service planned a new lookout in the Merritt district in 1951.
evidence.quote: The B.C. Forest Service expects to establish a new lookout in Merritt district this year.

evidence.supports: Hamilton Mountain is a 4,950 ft peak about three miles southwest of the west end of Douglas Lake.
evidence.quote: a 4950 foot peak about three miles southwest of the west end of Douglas Lake

evidence.supports: The lookout was expected to be in operation the following week in July 1951.
evidence.quote: The new Forest Service lookout on Hamilton Mountain will be in operation next week

evidence.supports: A permanent pre-fabricated building was expected later in the season, after a tent was used first.
evidence.quote: before the end of the season it is expected to have a permanent pre-fabricated building constructed.

evidence.supports: The planned lookout attendant was Johnny Wenlock of Chu Chua.
evidence.quote: Johnny Wenlock of Chu Chua will man the lookout.

evidence.supports: A tent was to be used first, before a permanent building was constructed.
evidence.quote: a tent will be used at first

evidence.supports: The site was expected to give an excellent view over the upper Nicola River watershed.
evidence.quote: It commands an excellent view of the upper Nicola River watershed

evidence.supports: Early detection of fires was expected to mean smaller fires.
evidence.quote: early detection of fires will be possible which in turn will result in smaller fires

evidence.supports: The lookout was expected to bring considerable savings in firefighting costs.
evidence.quote: with considerable saving in fire-fighting costs

evidence.supports: The lookout is described as abandoned, and landowners have stopped public access up the service road.
evidence.quote: The abandoned fire lookout on Mt Hamilton (Quilchena, BC) seldom sees visitors since the surrounding landowners have stopped public access up the service road.

evidence.supports: The tower is surrounded by private property with no public access.
evidence.quote: Hamilton Fire Lookout (Merritt area, surrounded by private property, no public access)

evidence.supports: The guide lists towers as confirmed or believed to still be standing, and includes Hamilton.
evidence.quote: Below is a region-by-region inventory of the towers confirmed or believed to still be standing.

evidence.supports: The guide's inventory lists Hamilton as surrounded by private property with no public access.
evidence.quote: Hamilton (Merritt area — surrounded by private property, no public access)

evidence.supports: Firelookout.ca records the site as private property with no access.

sources.title: Fire Lookouts of British Columbia: History, Hikes & Where to Stay

notes_for_editor: The 1951 build is known only from Merritt Herald reports of plans (May: expects to establish; July: expected in operation the next week). No source confirms completion, the staffing that followed, or when the lookout was abandoned. The metric height is a conversion of the 4950 ft in the source (about 1,509 m). The agency is the B.C. Forest Service as of 1951; the present owner or managing agency is not named in any source. Access is private and no route is suggested in the story on purpose. The Life is Adventure blog gives a hiking account; it was not used for route details. About five distinct pages were read and two WebSearch calls were used.
